memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The next day Moses took his seat to serve as judge for the people, and they
stood around him from morning till evening." - Ex 18:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One man, one chair, and a queue that lasts all day.

Picture it honestly. Moses sits down in the morning and does not get up until
evening. People stand in line for hours. Some of them wait all day and are still
waiting when the sun goes down.

Nobody planned this. It grew. Moses had been the only leader when they left
Egypt, and as the demands multiplied, he simply absorbed them one by one. That is
how most of us end up overloaded. Not through a single bad decision but through
a hundred small ones, each of which seemed reasonable.

Notice that Moses was doing something genuinely good. He was not wasting time.
He was serving people who needed help, and he was doing it faithfully.

That is what makes this kind of exhaustion so hard to address. If the work were
pointless, we would stop. Because it is worthwhile, we keep going, and the fact
that it is worthwhile becomes the reason we never examine it.

Sometimes the most spiritual question is not "Is this good work?" but "Is this
sustainable, and is it mine to do?"

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What good thing are you doing that has quietly become unsustainable?
2. When did you last examine your workload rather than just absorbing it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me the honesty to look at what I am carrying, even when all of it
seems worthwhile. Amen.
